units.text: The monitor in my dark bedroom went black, and glowing red text appeared: Hi Jack, I need a favor from you.
The internet was disconnected, yet the screen answered my thoughts.
It promised wealth if I moved an office plant.
Let us begin.
An entity called the Seer contacted me through my offline computer, claiming it saw all branching timelines.
Its first favor was simple: move a potted plant in my office lobby at eight seventeen.
An hour later, my boss tripped over the plant, violently twisting his ankle.
Unable to drive, he asked my favorite coworker, Allie, to take him to the hospital.
Minutes later, a speeding truck crushed their car, killing Allie instantly.
In horror, I wanted to smash the monitor, but the Seer said her death spared me betrayal.
The next morning, I was promoted to division manager with a fortune in bonuses.
Every monthly favor brought ruin to a stranger, but immense wealth and love to me.
A lottery favor ruined a stranger's family, while a parking favor led me to Donna, my future wife.
For twelve glorious years, my life was heaven on earth.
Then came the final favor: call a pizza parlor, let it ring three times, and hang up.
Thirty minutes later, a towering delivery brute arrived, glaring with fury when I had no cash tip.
Donna fell asleep on the couch, and I crept upstairs to the computer.
The screen lit up with the horrifying truth.
Every past favor was an engineered domino to turn that delivery boy into a weapon and bring him here tonight.
The screen read: He is downstairs right now, ending Donna's life at this exact second.
As heavy footsteps ascended the stairs, a soothing voice whispered in my mind: I gave you twelve magnificent years instead of eighty-five bitter, lonely ones.
The giant entered with a bloodstained blade.
The screen pulsed: Don't you have something to say to me, Jack?
With tears in my eyes, I whispered: Thank you.
Would you trade eighty-five bitter years for twelve perfect ones?
